title: B. Rectangles
statement:
You are given a binary grid$$^{∗}$$ $$G$$ of dimensions $$n $\times m$$$.

Let us define a rectangle as a tuple $$(u,d,l,r)$$ that satisfies the following conditions:

Then, the area of a rectangle $$(u,d,l,r)$$ is defined as $$(d-u+1) $\cdot (r-l+1)$$$.

For example, consider the following binary grid given below.

$$$\begin{matrix} 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \end{matrix}$$$

Here, you may see two rectangles $$(1,2,1,3)$$ and $$(1,3,3,5)$$$$^{†}$$, each of which has area $$6$$ and $$9$$, respectively.

For each cell $$(i,j)$$, find the minimum area of any rectangle $$(u,d,l,r)$$ such that $$u $\leq i \leq d$$$ and $$l $\leq j \leq r$$$.

$$^{∗}$$A binary grid is a grid where each cell contains $$0$$ or $$1$$. The cell on the $$j$$-th column of the $$i$$-th row is denoted as cell $$(i,j)$$.

$$^{†}$$Note that these are the only rectangles in the grid; for example, $$(1,1,1,5)$$ is not a rectangle as it does not satisfy $$u \lt d$$.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$t$$ ($$1 $\leq t \leq 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers $$n$$ and $$m$$ ($$2 $\leq n,m$$$, $$n$\cdot m \leq 250\,000$$$).

Each of the $$n$$ following lines contains a string of length $$m$$ denoting the $$i$$-th row of $$G$$ ($$G_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$$).

It is guaranteed that the sum of $$n$\cdot m$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$250\,000$$.
